role: independent static implementation/review; no VM or native execution by this reviewer
implemented: Add cpu/chaomofa-tcg-x87-selectors-v1 subsection, version/minimum 1, two uint16 FCS/FDS fields. Always emitted for TCG, including zero, for each registered x86 CPU.
TCG always emits existing cpu/fpop_ip_dp subsection, including all-zero FOP/FIP/FDP. Existing subsection field order, types and version unchanged.

TCG cpu_post_load reconstructs cc_src, cc_op=CC_OP_EFLAGS and df from loaded EFLAGS, leaving materialized EFLAGS intact. This prevents immediate cpu_compute_eflags from ORing stale B condition/DF bits into restored A before exec_enter.

xen_load pairs migration yank instance registration with the existing incoming-state destroy. Registration failure closes only its newly opened file and returns an error; successful registration is destroyed on both loader success and loader error.

wire_contract.identity_enforcement: Caller must authenticate exact binary SHA, source/patch manifest, configuration, CPU model/features/topology, guest bytes and checkpoint SHA before loading. The subsection name is not a binary identity attestation.
wire_contract.compatibility: Old readers reject the new unknown subsection. New readers can accept old streams missing it and cannot recover selectors absent from those streams; such streams are outside this contract. No cross-build or old-stock restore claim.
wire_contract.remaining_optional_fields: Same-process loading does not reset CPU/device state. Other optional subsections can still leave stale nonzero B fields if A omitted them. The patch closes this issue only for FCS/FDS and FOP/FIP/FDP; constrain B to explicitly exercised, serialized fields.

api_findings.availability: QAPI and handlers have no Xen-accelerator-only check. Actual configured devices can still block migration; first QMP error must reject.
api_findings.save: Explicit live=false. Caller first stops all VPs. Save synchronizes registered CPU states and writes early/non-iterable CPU/device sections, not RAM iteration or block contents. If initially running it restarts; the pre-stopped protocol avoids that.
api_findings.load: Rejects running VM; no machine reset; calls full loader and incoming cleanup; does not itself vm_start. Require query-status not running and exported stopped=true for both VPs after load. Serialized global RUNNING metadata alone is not live runstate.
api_findings.why_cli: Device save writes basic header but no configuration or VMDESC. Default loader expects configuration and otherwise rejects; optional VMDESC read at EOF emits a diagnostic. Both omissions are deliberate for this device-only route.
api_findings.cpu_coverage: CPU common plus legacy x86 VMState registered per CPU index. Main state includes full target-width GPR/RIP/EFLAGS, segments/table base, CRs, DR array, FP80 slots, CW/SW/TOP/empty tags, MXCSR and XMM. New selectors complete this particular missing storage pair, not architecture semantics or all optional state.
api_findings.post_load: Common CPU restores halted/interrupt state and invalidates TLB; TLB helper also invalidates per-CPU jump cache synchronously. x86 restores FP TOP/tags/status, SSE status and hardware BP_CPU watch/breakpoint registrations. GDB breakpoints are not serialized or removed by BP_CPU cleanup.
api_findings.tb_limit: No general TB cache flush was found on this route. Retaining immutable guest RAM/code with unchanged mapping is required for this probe. It does not authorize changed-memory restore or cold replay.
api_findings.ram_limit: RAM load_setup allocates receive bookkeeping but device stream contains no RAM pages. Guest RAM and block contents are not rolled back. A register-only interval in a nonpaged, IF=0 guest avoids explicit memory writes, but whole-machine DMA/timer/resource state is not thereby proved unchanged.
api_findings.mxcsr_limit: Current diagnostic query materializes lazy SSE exception flags before save. This reviewed sequence queries all CPUs before saving; generic save API correctness for arbitrary unqueried SIMD exceptions is not established.
api_findings.failure_semantics: Load is not atomic. A parsing/post-load failure may leave partially modified CPU/devices; terminate the owned microguest after failure, do not continue as if A or B were intact.

first_native_failure_review.observed: save completed; first xen-load aborts at util/yank.c:105 assert(entry). No successful restore or continuation can be inferred.
first_native_failure_review.root_cause: qmp_xen_load_devices_state lacks yank_register_instance while its migration_incoming_state_destroy unconditionally unregisters. Ordinary load_snapshot explicitly pairs registration. v4 patch addresses this precise mismatch; runtime result remains parent-owned.

probe_review.decoded_interval: NOP plus FNINIT/FLD/FADD/MOVDQA/LDMXCSR/GPR arithmetic and STC/STD/CLD; no explicit RAM store between A/B. Rich and inverse perturb pointer/selector zero cases, physical tags, XMM0/MXCSR, GPR and condition/DF flags.
required_before_operations: Verify schema, VP identities and both VPs stopped; exact A before save and exact B before load.
Assert CR0.PG=0 and IF=0 before A/B protocol; do not merely infer from instruction bytes.
Read/hash owned 0x100000..0x105000 bytes at A, B, after-load and second B; reject mismatch. This proves only that bounded region.
Preserve first raw before/after state and QMP errors; compare all exported fields, all FP80 slots including empty payloads, and both VPs.
Require after-save state identical A; immediate after-load identical A before resuming; re-execution identical B; only then remove B breakpoint and require exact output and exit.
probe_review.coverage_limit: Matching unchanged CR/segment/DR fields proves preservation in this fixture, not perturbation coverage. Only BSP executes; VP1 preservation is not SMP execution. No game, Windows, native handles or arbitrary CPU restore acceptance.
